metadata.description: A ZFS dataset or zvol, as a dialect of Volume: what a consumer orders is a volume (capacity, access mode, filesystem or block) and ZFS is how one host-local provider realizes it — a mounted dataset when volume_mode is filesystem, a zvol when block. Carved from a StoragePool, it cannot outlive its pool; datasets nest. Inherits capacity (the quota or volsize), access_mode and volume_mode from Volume; adds the ZFS-native mountpoint, reported usage and passthrough properties. Snapshot and replication policy is Policy (the control plane), not stored here. Grounded in OpenZFS (dataset).

capacity.description: Requested capacity, Kubernetes quantity form (e.g. 100Gi). SNIA Swordfish CapacityBytes maps here.

volume_mode.description: Filesystem-mounted vs raw block device (Kubernetes PVC volumeMode).

storage_class.description: Resource reference to a StorageClass (common-elements §2.5, DCM ADR-025). Authored by handle; deferred resolution supported (claim-before-define).

retain_on_release.description: Reclaim policy: true = Retain (keep data after the consumer releases it), false = Delete.

layout_entry.description: The StorageLayout entry name this volume realizes — the join key paired with the realizes_layout_entry edge. Instance edges carry no qualifier (the dependencies[] of a record is a closed shape, state-record.schema.json), so the entry binding lives HERE: set exactly when realizes_layout_entry is declared, matching an entry name in the referenced layout. Reconvergence joins on this value to populate the layout's realized_volumes map.

mountpoint.description: Filesystem mountpoint when volume_mode is filesystem (e.g. /export/gitlab); "none"/"-" if unmounted.

used.description: Space consumed as the provider reports it.

properties.description: Provider-passthrough dataset properties (compression, recordsize, mountpoint inheritance, etc.).

volume_handle.description: Provider volume handle/id once Realized (CSI volumeHandle / Swordfish Volume Id).

attached.description: Whether the volume is currently attached to a consumer.

relationships.name: provisioned_by
relationships.description: The StorageCluster that provisions this volume (binds its block_storage_class / file_storage_class output). A volume cannot outlive its provisioning cluster.

relationships.name: attaches_to
relationships.description: The consumer(s) this volume is attached to (RWX volumes attach to many). attaches_to is the same relation IPAddress uses for interface attachment — the consumable-resource-to-consumer edge.

relationships.name: realizes_layout_entry
relationships.description: Declared consumer-side (consumers declare what they consume — the layout never lists its consumers): this volume realizes one named entry of a StorageLayout, joining on the entry's stable name carried in spec.layout_entry (the edge itself carries no qualifier).

relationships.name: pool
relationships.description: The pool this dataset is carved from; the dataset cannot outlive its pool.

relationships.name: parent_dataset
relationships.description: The parent dataset in the hierarchy (e.g. aspen/nc/data → aspen/nc), when nested.

relationships.name: host
relationships.description: The host the pool (and thus this dataset) is local to.

adopts.role: consumable-volume request vocabulary (capacity, accessModes, volumeMode, storageClass, reclaimPolicy)
storage-volume-as-asset vocabulary (CapacityBytes, AccessCapabilities) — same family as StorageCluster
dataset vocabulary (mountpoint, used, quota, properties, hierarchy)

context.purpose: Models a ZFS dataset or zvol carved from a host-local pool — the mounted filesystem or block device host workloads use.
context.plain_description: A volume realized by ZFS on one host: its `volume_mode` says whether it is a mounted dataset (`filesystem`) or a zvol block device (`block`); its `capacity` is the quota or volsize; `mountpoint`, reported `used` and passthrough `properties` are the ZFS-native details. It is what a podman container or host service bind-mounts, so it is the storage node those workloads depend on. Volumes nest (parent chains) and cannot outlive the pool they are carved from. Snapshot and replication policy is orchestration, not stored here.
use_when: You need host services and containers tied to the specific dataset they store on, so the dataset outlives them in shutdown order.
You need the pool → dataset → workload chain explicit for capacity and migration planning.
not_for: The pool it is carved from — StoragePool owns the drives and redundancy.
Cluster-provisioned volumes a platform attaches — order at Volume, or a Type of another provisioner; a ZFS volume is host-local.
A network share exported to other machines — FileShare exposes storage; this is the local storage itself.
works_with: StoragePool — the pool the volume is carved from.
Machine.BareMetalHost — the host the volume is local to.
Volume.ZFS — the parent dataset, when nested.
